cold_email.subject: Interest in Part-Time Educator / Westport — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear lululemon Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Part-Time Educator / Westport opportunity with lululemon at lululemon.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Agent Training & Development Specialist — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Landstar Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Agent Training & Development Specialist opportunity with Landstar at Landstar.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Customer Service Associate I — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Dollar Tree Stores Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Customer Service Associate I opportunity with Dollar Tree Stores at Dollar Tree Stores.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Customer Service Associate I — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Dollar Tree Stores Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Customer Service Associate I opportunity with Dollar Tree Stores at Dollar Tree Stores.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in GI Biobank Research Technician — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Dana-Farber Cancer Institute Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the GI Biobank Research Technician opportunity with Dana-Farber Cancer Institute at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Research Data Coordinator - Burnsville — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Comprehensive Cancer Centers of Nevada Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Research Data Coordinator - Burnsville opportunity with Comprehensive Cancer Centers of Nevada at Comprehensive Cancer Centers of Nevada.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Research Scientist/Engineer 1 — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear University of Washington Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Research Scientist/Engineer 1 opportunity with University of Washington at University of Washington.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

Dear University of Oklahoma Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Student Recruiter (Fall) opportunity with University of Oklahoma at University of Oklahoma.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in 2026-27 Educational Assistant - Behavior & Instruction - Part-Time - 4.25 hpd - Douglas Gardens Elementary School — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear SchoolSpring Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the 2026-27 Educational Assistant - Behavior & Instruction - Part-Time - 4.25 hpd - Douglas Gardens Elementary School opportunity with SchoolSpring at SchoolSpring.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Educational Technician Content Specialist - STEAM LAB - WC (007-27) — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear North Carolina Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Educational Technician Content Specialist - STEAM LAB - WC (007-27) opportunity with North Carolina Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services at North Carolina Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Tutor (APU 4-Nights) — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear NEMERA Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Tutor (APU 4-Nights) opportunity with NEMERA at NEMERA.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Marketing Coordinator, Kohler — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Kohler Hospitality Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Marketing Coordinator, Kohler opportunity with Kohler Hospitality at Kohler Hospitality.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

Dear Greater Somerset County YMCA Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Youth Program Coordinator opportunity with Greater Somerset County YMCA at Greater Somerset County YMCA.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Child Development Center Aide - Part Time (Open) — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear East Side Union High School District Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Child Development Center Aide - Part Time (Open) opportunity with East Side Union High School District at East Side Union High School District.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Lab Analyst — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Cardinal Health Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Lab Analyst opportunity with Cardinal Health at Cardinal Health.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.body:
Dear Aimbridge Hospitality Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Holiday Inn & Suites Nashville Downtown - Engineer opportunity with Aimbridge Hospitality at Aimbridge Hospitality.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

Dear UnitedHealth Group Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Laboratory Administrative Coordinator opportunity with UnitedHealth Group at UnitedHealth Group.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. cold_email.subject: Interest in Research Associate — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Parexel Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Research Associate opportunity with Parexel at Parexel.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Customer Service Associate I — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Dollar Tree Stores Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Customer Service Associate I opportunity with Dollar Tree Stores at Dollar Tree Stores.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Substitute Teaching Pool - Founders Classical Academy of Schertz — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Responsive Education Solutions Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Substitute Teaching Pool - Founders Classical Academy of Schertz opportunity with Responsive Education Solutions at Responsive Education Solutions.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

jobs.title: Associate Talent Partner, Early Career Recruiting
jobs.description: The Role: Moderna is entering its next phase of evolution, and attracting world-class early career talent is critical to fueling our mission to deliver the greatest possible impact to patients. We are seeking an Associate Talent Partner, Early Career Recruiting to deliver recruitment and hiring of interns and co-ops across the company. In this role, you will execute the strategy that shapes how emerging talent experiences Moderna – from first impression through university partnerships, to recruitment, selection, offer, and preparing for onboarding. As an Early Career recruiter, you will operate with significant autonomy, partnering with senior business and HR leaders across the company to understand intern and co-op opportunities in the business and bring them to life. This role is ideal for a resourceful, agile recruiter who can flex between attracting and evaluating candidates, partnering with top-tier universities, and presenting to senior leaders – someone who thrives in a fast-paced, ever-evolving, mission-driven environment. Here’s What You’ll Do: Partner with senior stakeholders to understand hiring needs, align on pipeline priorities, and organize Early Career talent planning across functions. Drive accountability for Early Career hiring across stakeholders. Deliver a best-in-class Early Career experience, delivering end-to-end recruitment for internship and co-op roles, including talent attraction, sourcing, screening, hiring manager partnership, candidate experience, and offers. Drive campus engagement and university partnership that expands Moderna’s reach across a diverse range of top-tier universities. Guide business teams in delivering high-impact events. Lead Moderna’s presence at campus and virtual events that build awareness and excitement among emerging talent. Represent Early Careers in senior-level conversations and reports; inform leaders through data, insights, and compelling storytelling. Act as a culture ambassador who brings Moderna’s values to life in every candidate touchpoint. Here’s What You’ll Need (Minimum Qualifications): Bachelor’s Degree At least 3 years’ experience in Campus Recruiting, Talent Acquisition, or University Admissions. Strong recruiting skills and the ability to creatively identify and engage exceptional emerging talent. Strong written and verbal communication skills; confident presenting to senior leaders. Excellent detail orientation; demonstrated strength in planning and follow through of complex initiatives or projects. Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, highly collaborative environment with significant autonomy. Here’s What You’ll Bring to the Table (Preferred Qualifications): Experience with ATS/CRM tools such as Workday and Handshake. Demonstrated success engaging talent through diversity-focused partnerships, university associations, student groups, HBCUs, HSIs, and professional organizations. Enthusiasm for optimizing or transforming workflow or processes through AI and/or automation. Pay & Benefits At Moderna, we believe that when you feel your best, you can do your best work. That’s why our benefits and well-being resources are designed to support you—at work, at home, and everywhere in between. Competitive healthcare, plus voluntary benefit programs to support your unique needs A holistic approach to well-being, with access to fitness, mindfulness, and mental health support Family planning benefits, including fertility, adoption, and surrogacy support Generous paid time off, including vacation, volunteer days, sabbatical, global recharge days, and a discretionary year-end shutdown Savings and investments to help you plan for the future Location-specific perks and extras The salary range for this role is $89,900.00 - $143,800.00. This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An individual’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, performance, and business or organizational needs. The successful candidate may be eligible for an annual discretionary bonus, other incentive compensation, or equity award, subject to company plan eligibility criteria and individual performance. About Moderna Since our founding in 2010, we have aspired to build the leading mRNA technology platform, the infrastructure to reimagine how medicines are created and delivered, and a world-class team. We believe in giving our people a platform to change medicine and an opportunity to change the world. By living our mission, values, and mindsets every day, our people are the driving force behind our scientific progress and our culture. Together, we are creating a culture of belonging and building an organization that cares deeply for our patients, our employees, the environment, and our communities. We are proud to have been recognized as a Science Magazine Top Biopharma Employer, a Fast Company Best Workplace for Innovators, and a Great Place to Work in the U.S. If you want to make a difference and join a team that is changing the future of medicine, we invite you to visit modernatx.com/careers to learn more about our current opportunities. Our Working Model As we build our company, we have always believed an in-person culture is critical to our success. Moderna champions the significant benefits of in-office collaboration by embracing a 70/30 work model. This 70% in-office structure helps to foster a culture rich in innovation, teamwork, and direct mentorship. Join us in shaping a world where every interaction is an opportunity to learn, contribute, and make a meaningful impact. Moderna is a smoke-free, alcohol-free, and drug-free work environment. Equal Opportunities Moderna is committed to equal employment opportunity and non-discrimination for all employees and qualified applicants without regard to a person's race, color, sex, gender identity or expression, age, religion, national origin, ancestry or citizenship, ethnicity, disability, military or protected veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, marital or familial status, or any other personal characteristic protected under applicable law. jobs.description: Career Category Operations Job Description Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do. Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. With our focus on four therapeutic areas –Oncology, Inflammation, General Medicine, and Rare Disease– we reach millions of patients each year. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline of medicines to treat cancer, heart disease, inflammatory conditions, rare diseases, and obesity and obesity-related conditions. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives. Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career. Data Scientist What you will do Let’s do this. Let’s change the world. In this vital role you will be at the forefront of digital transformation in the biopharmaceutical industry. This team provides thought leadership and enhances capabilities for a data based workflow, digital threads and digital twins. The Data Automation Data Scientist will play a pivotal role in advancing digital transformation by driving the development, integration, and adoption of digital automation across enterprise platforms, including Product Lifecycle Management (PLM), Electronic Laboratory Notebooks (ELN), and enterprise data platforms. You will collaborate with cross-functional teams to deliver impactful digital solutions while maintaining the digital thread across engineering testing, laboratory operations, and data analytics to ensure seamless data integration, accessibility, and traceability. You will also partner closely with internal stakeholders to understand business needs, optimize workflows, and deliver scalable digital capabilities. Serve as the Subject Matter Expert (SME) for automated test data collection from digital laboratory, electronic lab notebook (ELN) and testing solutions. Lead the implementation, adoption, support, and continuous improvement of digital data capture capabilities. ​ Ensure collection of FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable) laboratory and engineering data by promoting data integrity, standardization, metadata management, and data governance across enterprise systems. Maintain the digital thread by integrating design, verification testing, and laboratory data across the product lifecycle to improve traceability, accessibility, and collaboration. Partner with cross-functional stakeholders to gather business requirements, optimize laboratory workflows, validate system enhancements, and deliver scalable digital solutions. Drive digital transformation and user adoption by performing system testing, delivering end-user training, managing enhancement requests, and ensuring compliance with Design Control, GMP, GDP, and applicable quality requirements. Query, analyze, and visualize laboratory and engineering data to generate actionable insights, improve process performance, and support data-driven decision making. What we expect of you We are all different, yet we all use our unique contributions to serve patients. The professional we seek is a leader with these qualifications. Basic Qualifications: Master’s degree OR Bachelor’s degree and 2 years of Data Scientist/Engineering experience OR Associate’s degree and 6 years of Data Scientist/Engineering experience OR High school diploma / GED and 8 years of Data Scientist/Engineering experience Preferred Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree or Advanced Degree. in engineering, Mechanical, Biomedical, bioengineering or Chemical Engineering or a related technical field 1–2 years of experience in the medical device, pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or other regulated industry. Experience with Electronic Laboratory Notebooks (ELN) , Laboratory Information Management Systems (LIMS), Product Lifecycle Management (PLM), such as Biova Onelab, 3DExperience, or similar enterprise digital platforms. Experience leading or supporting the implementation, rollout, and adoption of digital tools and laboratory workflows. Experience supporting engineering verification testing, laboratory operations, or product development activities in a regulated environment. Working knowledge of the automation of laboratory test equipment engineering data . Knowledge of Design Control, ISO 13485, GMP, GDP, and applicable regulatory requirements for medical devices and combination products. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to query, analyze, interpret, and communicate data-driven insights. Proficiency in SQL, Python (R is a plus), and business intelligence tools such as Power BI or Tableau to query, analyze, visualize, and communicate data-driven insights. Strong technical aptitude with the ability to translate business requirements into scalable digital solutions and collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams. What you can expect of us As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. From our competitive benefits to our collaborative culture, we’ll support your journey every step of the way. jobs.title: Scientist, Analytical Development
jobs.description: Working with Us Challenging. Meaningful. Life-changing. Those aren’t words that are usually associated with a job. But working at Bristol Myers Squibb is anything but usual. Here, uniquely interesting work happens every day, in every department. From optimizing a production line to the latest breakthroughs in cell therapy, this is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it. You’ll get the chance to grow and thrive through opportunities uncommon in scale and scope, alongside high-achieving teams. Take your career farther than you thought possible. Bristol Myers Squibb recognizes the importance of balance and flexibility in our work environment. We offer a wide variety of competitive benefits, services and programs that provide our employees with the resources to pursue their goals, both at work and in their personal lives. Read more: careers.bms.com/working-with-us . What if the hardest analytical problem you've ever faced was actually the most important one you'll ever solve? Not important in a "this will look great on my CV" kind of way. Important in a "this gets a life-changing medicine to a patient faster" kind of way. That's the level of stakes we're working at every day in BMS's Chemical Process Development team and it's why we're looking for someone who genuinely loves the challenge. This Role Is For You If... You're the kind of scientist who gets genuinely excited when something doesn't work the way it should. Who sees a tricky separation problem and thinks "let me figure this out" rather than "let me pass this along." Who reads about 2DLC or capillary electrophoresis not because you have to but because you actually find it fascinating. If that's you - keep reading . The Role As a Scientist in Analytical Development , you'll be embedded within Chemical Process Development ( CPD ) project teams, working shoulder-to-shoulder with organic chemists and chemical engineers on some of the most scientifically complex drug candidates in BMS's portfolio - spanning small molecules, ADCs, peptides, and oligonucleotides . This isn't a support role in the background. You'll be a core contributor , providing the analytical insights that directly shape route selection, process optimisation, and scale-up decisions. The data you generate, the methods you develop and the solutions you bring to the table will have a direct line to clinical outcomes. What You'll Be Doing — and What It Really Means for You Developing and validating fit-for-purpose analytical methods You won't be handed a standard operating procedure and told to follow it. You'll be building the methodologies yourself - sharpening your technical toolkit on some of the most complex molecules in modern drug development. Applying innovative separation techniques like 2DLC and SFC You'll have the freedom and the resources to explore cutting-edge analytical approaches - building expertise that's genuinely sought after across the entire pharmaceutical industry. Implementing automation and improving continuous manufacturing monitoring This is where analytical science meets the future. You'll be at the forefront of integrating automation, AI/ML, and data science into real pharmaceutical workflows - skills that will define the next generation of analytical scientists. Transferring methods to support timely clinical API batch release There's a direct thread between the method you develop and a patient receiving a clinical trial dose. That's a thread worth pulling. Collaborating across matrixed teams within CPD and broader Product Development You'll build relationships across disciplines - chemistry, engineering, regulatory, manufacturing - giving you a breadth of perspective and a professional network that's genuinely rare. Publishing and presenting your work externally BMS actively encourages you to share your science with the wider world. Your work here won't just sit in an internal database - it has the potential to advance the field. What You'll Gain Let's be direct about what this role gives you : Technical depth AND breadth - You'll develop expertise across a diverse portfolio of modalities (small molecules, ADCs, peptides, oligonucleotides) that most analytical scientists simply never get access to in a single role A clear growth path - BMS explicitly invests in your advancement, whether that's moving up the technical ladder as a specialist or stepping into an analytical leadership role on project teams. The trajectory is yours to shape Cutting-edge tools and techniques - Access to automation, AI/ML capabilities, and advanced analytical technologies that keep your skills firmly at the leading edge of the industry Visibility and recognition - Opportunities to publish, present, and be seen as a thought leader - both inside BMS and in the broader scientific community Work that echoes beyond the lab - Every method you develop, every process you optimise, every clinical batch you help release brings a drug candidate closer to the patients waiting for it What You'll Bring A PhD or Master's degree in Analytical or Organic Chemistry (practical, hands-on experience is key - qualifications are evaluated in context of your full background) Solid experience with chromatographic and/or spectroscopic techniques An interest or working knowledge of data science, AI/ML, or programming applied to analytical chemistry (highly valued, not just a nice-to-have) Experience navigating matrixed, cross-functional teams - you know how to collaborate across disciplines and make it look effortless A genuine can-do attitude - you adapt, you learn, you push forward even when the problem is stubborn An unwavering commitment to safety and the highest scientific standards The Kind of Place You'll Be Doing It BMS's Chemical Process Development function is built around the belief that world-class analytical science isn't a service function - it's a strategic differentiator . You'll be joining a team that actively partners across the organisation, that invests in its people's growth, and that genuinely celebrates scientific curiosity. Here, your ideas will land. Your instincts will be trusted. And your best work will find its way to patients who need it. Ready to Bring Your Analytical Best to Work That Actually Matters? If you've been waiting for a role that challenges you technically, rewards your curiosity, and connects your science to something truly meaningful — this is it. We'd love to hear from you. #LI-Hybrid If you come across a role that intrigues you but doesn’t perfectly line up with your resume, we encourage you to apply anyway. You could be one step away from work that will transform your life and career. Uniquely Interesting Work, Life-changing Careers With a single vision as inspiring as “Transforming patients’ lives through science™ ”, every BMS employee plays an integral role in work that goes far beyond ordinary. Each of us is empowered to apply our individual talents and unique perspectives in a supportive culture, promoting global participation in clinical trials, while our shared values of passion, innovation, urgency, accountability, inclusion and integrity bring out the highest potential of each of our colleagues. On-site Protocol BMS has an occupancy structure that determines where an employee is required to conduct their work. This structure includes site-essential, site-by-design, field-based and remote-by-design jobs. The occupancy type that you are assigned is determined by the nature and responsibilities of your role: Site-essential roles require 100% of shifts onsite at your assigned facility. Site-by-design roles may be eligible for a hybrid work model with at least 50% onsite at your assigned facility. For these roles, onsite presence is considered an essential job function and is critical to collaboration, innovation, productivity, and a positive Company culture. For field-based and remote-by-design roles the ability to physically travel to visit customers, patients or business partners and to attend meetings on behalf of BMS as directed is an essential job function. Applicants can request a reasonable workplace accommodation/adjustment prior to accepting a job offer. If you require reasonable accommodations/adjustments in completing this application, or in any part of the recruitment process, direct your inquiries to adastaffingsupport@bms.com . cold_email.subject: Interest in Scientist, Analytical Development — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Bristol Myers Squibb Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Scientist, Analytical Development opportunity with Bristol Myers Squibb at Bristol Myers Squibb.

I am especially interested in building scalable data systems that let research and clinical teams use biological data reliably. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, I have built API-driven and Snakemake-based pipelines, automated SQL workflows, and worked across both scientific and software contexts.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: Data Scientist
jobs.description: Career Category Research Job Description Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do. Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. With our focus on four therapeutic areas –Oncology, Inflammation, General Medicine, and Rare Disease– we reach millions of patients each year. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline of medicines to treat cancer, heart disease, inflammatory conditions, rare diseases, and obesity and obesity-related conditions. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives. Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career. Data Scientist As a Data Scientist , you will design, develop, and implement scalable data engineering, machine learning (ML), and analytics solutions that accelerate Clinical Development and advance therapies for patients. You will act in support the Center for Design & Analysis, partnering with data scientists and cross-functional teams to translate business requirements into robust data pipelines, analytical tools, and visualization solutions. You will contribute to the implementation and continuous improvement of innovative analytics capabilities, helping to optimize methods, algorithms, and processes while ensuring solutions are reliable, scalable, and aligned with Amgen's quality and compliance standards. Responsibilities: Collaborating with research scientist and other data scientists to develop AI and advanced analytics solution to speed drug research and development. Designing, writing, and testing data / ML pipelines and other advanced analytic / visualization solutions Collect business requirements / user stories for new or enhancements to existing analytic solutions Train users in the use of solutions provided by the CfDA Data Science organization Contribute to process improvement initiatives Adhere to Amgen Policies, SOPs, and other controlled documents. Participate in the development and review of CfDA Data Sciences Policies, SOPs, and other controlled documents. Participate in external professional organizations, conferences and/or meetings. Accountabilities: Contribute to the implementation of internally developed and externally provided analytic solutions Participate in the development of innovative and effective approaches to solve client's analytics problems and communicate results & methodologies Recommend ongoing improvements to methods and algorithms that generate analytic insights Win What we expect of you We are all different, yet we all use our unique contributions to serve patients. Basic Qualifications Doctorate degree PhD OR PharmD OR MD OR Master’s degree and 3 years of related experience OR Bachelor’s degree and 5 years of related experience Preferred Qualifications MS or PhD in Statistics/Biostatistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Data Science, Physics, Informatics, Life Sciences, or quantitative related field. A proven ability to write robust code in R / Python A working understanding of common machine learning algorithms and approaches (NNs, RF classifiers, Ensemble methods, NLP etc.) and when to use them. Proficiency in Linux operating system and associated shell commands. Experience working effectively in a globally dispersed team environment. Drug Development (pre-, early, late and/or observational) in related industries or academic research) Experience working with: Distributed compute / data technology (e.g., Spark, Python Dask) DevOps frameworks (e.g., Git) Building and deploying analytic solutions in a cloud environment Entrepreneurial mindset with ability to self-direct A translator able to communicate complex concepts to a non-technical audience What you can expect of us As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. The Role As a Formulation Scientist within our Oral Product Development group, you'll be at the heart of turning BMS's most promising small molecule drug candidates into real, manufacturable medicines - from first-in-human all the way through to commercial readiness. Day to day, you'll be designing and developing oral formulations, solving the complex challenges of bioavailability and stability, and working closely with colleagues across Drug Product, Analytical, API, Quality, and Regulatory functions — both at BMS sites and with external manufacturing partners (CMOs). You won't just be executing tasks. You'll be contributing to strategy, shaping how drug products are developed and controlled, and leaving a visible mark on the projects you're assigned to. Real patients. Real impact. Evaluating bioavailability, stability, and processability solutions You'll tackle some of the most technically interesting problems in pharmaceutical development and build a depth of expertise that's genuinely rare in the industry. Collaborating across functions and sites You'll build a network that spans R&D, regulatory, quality, and manufacturing — giving you visibility and relationships that accelerate your career far beyond a single discipline. Contributing to drug development process You'll get exposure to how scientific data supports the regulatory journey of a drug, building a foundation for understanding the end-to-end development process over time. Our work spans enterprise workflows, agent experiences, integrations, identity, administration, security, governance, and deployment. You will translate customer needs, competitive dynamics, and product priorities into actionable plans, influence architectural direction, and deliver durable capabilities across application, platform, and infrastructure layers. The role requires deep technical fluency, strong product judgment, and the ability to move between hands-on execution and broader enterprise strategy. This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL: - Drive technical strategy and execution for enterprise product and AI workflow initiatives, from design through implementation, launch, customer rollout, and iteration. - Partner with engineering teams to influence architectural direction, interface definitions, and implementation tradeoffs across full-stack products, APIs, integrations, and shared platform systems. - Define the metrics, definitions, and analytical frameworks that leadership and every PM rely on, and own them as the single source of truth the Product org trusts. Fluent in SQL and comfortable in a modern data warehouse and BI tooling. You can go from raw data to a defensible answer yourself, not just direct others to do it. Professional use of AI tools such as Claude, including prompt design and putting AI into day-to-day analysis. jobs.description: Working with Us Challenging. Meaningful. Life-changing. Those aren’t words that are usually associated with a job. But working at Bristol Myers Squibb is anything but usual. Here, uniquely interesting work happens every day, in every department. From optimizing a production line to the latest breakthroughs in cell therapy, this is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it. You’ll get the chance to grow and thrive through opportunities uncommon in scale and scope, alongside high-achieving teams. Take your career farther than you thought possible. Bristol Myers Squibb recognizes the importance of balance and flexibility in our work environment. We offer a wide variety of competitive benefits, services and programs that provide our employees with the resources to pursue their goals, both at work and in their personal lives. Read more: careers.bms.com/working-with-us . Your code doesn't just run. It helps get life-changing medicines to patients. At Bristol Myers Squibb , we believe that behind every clean dataset, every validated submission package, every regulatory approval - there's a person who made it possible. That person could be you. We're looking for a Senior SDTM Statistical Programmer to join our team - someone who's ready to stop just delivering work and start genuinely leading it. So, what does this actually mean for you? You'll own something that matters - This isn't a role where you're handed a ticket and told to close it. You'll be the technical lead on assigned studies - shaping SDTM strategies from protocol review all the way through to global regulatory submission. You'll see the full picture and your fingerprints will be on deliverables that directly support medicines reaching patients around the world. You'll solve real, complex problems - not just tick boxes - Root cause analysis, cross-functional stakeholder collaboration, data integration from CRF and non-CRF sources - this role puts you at the intersection of science , data , and process . You'll build the kind of deep, end-to-end understanding that makes you genuinely invaluable, not just technically but strategically. You'll be at the frontier of where the industry is going - SDTM automation. Metadata-driven processes. Agentic AI workflows. These aren't buzzwords here - they're part of how we're transforming clinical data operations. You'll be actively engaged with emerging technologies , keeping your skills sharp and future-proof in a field that's evolving fast. You'll lead people, not just processes - You'll provide guidance and quality oversight to team members and manage CRO and vendor programming activities. Whether it's mentoring a junior programmer or partnering with a cross-functional study team, you'll develop the kind of leadership presence that accelerates careers - yours included. You'll contribute to global regulatory success - Every eCRT submission package you build, every Pinnacle 21 validation report you interpret, every SDTM specification you design — it all feeds into global regulatory filings and approvals . Few roles let you see your technical work translate so directly into real-world impact. What you'll bring to the table 4+ years of pharmaceutical or CRO experience as a SAS Programmer supporting clinical trials and regulatory submissions Deep expertise in CDISC/SDTM standards and a thorough understanding of the clinical development lifecycle Exceptional SAS programming skills (Base, Stat, Graph) and comfort working across complex, multi-source data environments Experience collaborating with cross-functional teams, managing timelines, and driving quality outcomes A degree in a relevant scientific discipline (BA/BS or above) The agility to adapt quickly, prioritise effectively, and lead through ambiguity — because clinical development rarely stands still Why BMS? Because here, your work is more than a deliverable. It's part of a mission to transform patients' lives through science . You'll work alongside some of the most talented minds in the industry, supported by a culture that values innovation, collaboration, and the courage to take on the hardest problems in medicine. You'll grow your technical expertise, build your leadership profile, and know — with certainty — that what you do every day genuinely matters. Ready to lead from the data up? Apply now and bring your SDTM expertise to work that changes lives #LI-Hybrid If you come across a role that intrigues you but doesn’t perfectly line up with your resume, we encourage you to apply anyway. You could be one step away from work that will transform your life and career. Uniquely Interesting Work, Life-changing Careers With a single vision as inspiring as “Transforming patients’ lives through science™ ”, every BMS employee plays an integral role in work that goes far beyond ordinary. Each of us is empowered to apply our individual talents and unique perspectives in a supportive culture, promoting global participation in clinical trials, while our shared values of passion, innovation, urgency, accountability, inclusion and integrity bring out the highest potential of each of our colleagues. The occupancy type that you are assigned is determined by the nature and responsibilities of your role: Site-essential roles require 100% of shifts onsite at your assigned facility. Site-by-design roles may be eligible for a hybrid work model with at least 50% onsite at your assigned facility. jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Cloud AI Partnerships
jobs.description: ABOUT THE TEAM The Product & Platform teams at OpenAI are responsible for delivering the company’s most impactful offerings—such as ChatGPT, our API platform, and new enterprise capabilities—to a global and diverse customer base. These systems must perform at scale and deliver exceptional experiences to developers, consumers, and businesses alike. Technical Program Managers at OpenAI play a key leadership role in scaling these efforts, partnering deeply with product, engineering, design, and go-to-market teams to bring ambitious ideas to life and ensure clarity and discipline in execution. ABOUT THE ROLE We are hiring a Technical Program Manager to support OpenAI's critical AI deployments across strategic cloud partners. This role is designed for a candidate who can operate as an end-to-end owner across internal engineering teams and external partner organizations. This role will drive the technical strategy and execution required to bring OpenAI models and platform capabilities into partner environments responsibly and at scale. The work spans engineering deliverables, shared roadmaps, model launch pipelines, technical integration, launch readiness, and post-launch follow-through. You will work closely with senior leaders across OpenAI engineering, infrastructure, product, safety, security, legal, finance, and go-to-market, as well as technical counterparts at our partners. The job is to turn broad partnership commitments into concrete execution plans, align both sides on what must land, and build repeatable mechanisms for launching OpenAI capabilities on third-party platforms. This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL: - Lead end-to-end execution for major cloud partner programs spanning model deployment, product integration, operational readiness, launch follow-through, and partner-platform adoption. - Own integrated technical roadmaps across OpenAI and partner teams, including milestones, dependencies, risks, resourcing needs, and the sequencing required to land joint commitments. - Own launch readiness across cloud partner platforms, including readiness checklists, blocker tracking, joint go/no-go reviews, and post-launch stability follow-through. - Act as a primary technical interface to partner engineering organizations, helping own the shared roadmap and day-to-day coordination on deployment, capacity, incidents, and open engineering issues. - Drive alignment across engineering, infrastructure, product, safety, security, legal, finance, and go-to-market teams so joint deliverables are well-scoped, sequenced, and executable. - Provide clear, transparent reporting on program status, issues, risks, and decisions required for senior leaders and stakeholders. - Convert open issues into prioritized plans that both OpenAI and partner teams can commit to, with clear owners, workbacks, and closure paths. - Help build repeatable and efficient development and launch pipelines for OpenAI models on partner platforms. YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU: - Bring substantial technical program management leadership across infrastructure, platform, or large-scale engineering work, with a track record of owning complex programs end to end. - Have led complex partner-facing programs where success required tight coordination across company boundaries, clear operating rhythms, and sustained follow-through. - Understand cloud architectures, AI/ML deployment, model serving, and the practical integration challenges of bringing advanced AI systems to production. - Direct experience with major cloud or AI platforms, including how models are integrated, launched, and onboarded for customers. - Familiarity with how foundation models are integrated, packaged, launched, and operated through partner platforms or marketplaces. - Experience with inference systems, model serving, accelerator-backed infrastructure, or distributed systems. - Can balance strategic priorities with rapid, high-quality execution in fast-moving environments. - Communicate crisply with engineers, executives, and external partners, and can create alignment without direct authority. - Thrive in ambiguous, scaling environments and can bring order to complex cross-functional work without losing pace. - Exercise strong judgment on risk, sequencing, and the difference between a target date and a credible launch plan. - Care about OpenAI's mission and about expanding responsible access to advanced AI systems. jobs.title: Product Marketing Operations Manager, Research
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic's model releases help us advance the frontier of both model intelligence and model safety. Each one brings research, product, policy, legal, communications, sales, and every part of marketing together around a single moment. You'll build and run the operating system behind that: the launch calendar, the plan of record for every deliverable, the path materials take through review, and execution on launch day. You'll treat the launch process itself as a product — one with users across the company, a quality bar, and a roadmap — and drive adoption through influence. This is a hands-on, high-ownership role on a lean product marketing team. When launch volume peaks, you'll contribute directly as a product marketer across all products and surfaces. If you've run launches where many moving parts had to converge at the same time, and you'd rather design the system than run it by hand, we'd like to meet you. Responsibilities Own the model launch calendar and sequencing across a broad portfolio of releases, coordinating timing with partner teams across marketing, product, and communications Own the plan of record for each launch — deliverables, owners, dependencies, and deadlines — and surface risks early enough to act on them Own the path launch materials take through review, partnering with legal, policy, research, and communications so reviews happen in the right sequence against dates people can plan to Drive decisions and alignment across senior cross-functional stakeholders without direct authority Own launch-day execution: sequencing, timing, access, and the operational readiness of everything that goes live together Own the internal resources our field teams reach for first, along with the operational side of enablement — scheduling, speakers, and materials logistics Develop and improve launch processes, playbooks, and operational frameworks that scale beyond any one launch Own launch retrospectives, recurring product communications, and — when volume requires it — launch materials themselves You may be a good fit if you Have owned launch or release operations end to end, and been accountable for launches landing on time and in good shape Have built or substantially improved a launch or release process Treat process as a product — you care whether people adopt what you build, and you measure it Background in product marketing, product operations, technical program management, and launch production all fit Work well when priorities and timelines shift, and can keep a complex plan coherent as details change Are effective at driving decisions across senior stakeholders without direct authority Have a technical background with the ability to understand and communicate complex AI concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences Write clearly, and can produce launch-ready material Are energized by ambiguity and moving fast in a rapidly evolving market Role-specific policy: For this role, we expect staff to be able to work from our San Francisco or New York office at least 2 days a week. We encourage you to apply even if you might need some flexibility for an interim period of time for relocation. Deadline to apply: None. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $255,000 — $320,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.
